en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Expiation (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Sahadhammika-vagga 75.
The Training Rule on the Palm-Blow.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, angry and displeased, raised their hands like clappers against the group-of-seventeen monks.
Struck by blows, they wept.
The monks said this:
“Friends, why are you weeping?
“Friends, these monks of the group-of-six, being angry and displeased, are brandishing their hand-fists at us.
Those monks who were few in desires... [and so on]... they complained, grumbled, and became indignant.
“How indeed can the group-of-six monks, being angry and displeased, raise their hands against the group-of-seventeen monks? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that you, being angry and displeased, raised your hands against the group-of-seventeen monks?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can you, foolish men, being angry and displeased, brandish a palm-leaf fan at the monks of the group of seventeen?
This, foolish men, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence…” [and so on].
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:
“Whatever monk, being angry and displeased with another monk, should raise his hand as a slap, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya). Whoever...
[the phrase] “whatever” means:
Whoever such as this … [as above] … is a bhikkhu … [as above] …; this is the kind of bhikkhu intended in this context.
"Of a bhikkhu" means of another bhikkhu.
"Angry and displeased" means...
Being dissatisfied, with a struck mind, and having become callous:
"He should throw up a palm-leaf fan" means that he raises up either his body or something connected to his body, even if it is only a lotus leaf; there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one who is fully ordained perceives another as fully ordained, and being angry and displeased, hurls a palm-leaf fan at them, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one who is fully ordained is of doubtful status, and being angry and displeased, hurls a palm-leaf fan at them, there is an offense of expiation.
If one who is fully ordained is perceived as not fully ordained, and being angry and displeased, hurls a palm-leaf fan at them, there is an offense of expiation.
If one is angry and displeased with one who has not received full ordination and hurls a palm-leaf fan at them, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one perceives someone who has not received full ordination as having received it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If one is in doubt regarding whether they have received full ordination, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If [the person] is not ordained and one perceives them as not ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if,
being harassed by someone, one raises a palm-leaf fan with the intention of escaping.
"In the case of one who is insane,
and in the case of the first offender.
The fifth training rule on throwing with the palm is concluded.
